tag_registry.label: Twin prime
tag_registry.definition: p-2 or p+2 is prime.

tag_registry.label: Cousin prime
tag_registry.definition: p-4 or p+4 is prime.

tag_registry.label: Sexy prime
tag_registry.definition: p-6 or p+6 is prime.

tag_registry.label: Prime triplet
tag_registry.definition: p is a member of a (p, p+2, p+6) or (p, p+4, p+6) triplet.

tag_registry.label: Prime quadruplet
tag_registry.definition: p is a member of a (p, p+2, p+6, p+8) quadruplet.

tag_registry.label: Prime quintuplet
tag_registry.definition: p is a member of a densest admissible 5-tuple.

tag_registry.label: Prime sextuplet
tag_registry.definition: p is a member of a (p, p+4, p+6, p+10, p+12, p+16) sextuplet.

tag_registry.label: Balanced prime
tag_registry.definition: p is the arithmetic mean of its neighbouring primes.

tag_registry.label: Isolated prime
tag_registry.definition: neither p-2 nor p+2 is prime.

tag_registry.label: Maximal-gap prime
tag_registry.definition: p opens a prime gap larger than every gap before it.

tag_registry.label: Strong prime
tag_registry.definition: p exceeds the mean of its neighbouring primes.

tag_registry.label: Weak prime
tag_registry.definition: p falls below the mean of its neighbouring primes.

tag_registry.label: Good prime
tag_registry.definition: p_n^2 > p_(n-i)*p_(n+i) for every i in [1, n-1].

tag_registry.label: Sophie Germain prime
tag_registry.definition: 2p+1 is also prime.

tag_registry.label: Safe prime
tag_registry.definition: (p-1)/2 is also prime.

tag_registry.label: Cunningham chain (length 3)
tag_registry.definition: p starts a chain p, 2p+1, 4p+3 of primes.

tag_registry.label: Cunningham chain (length 4+)
tag_registry.definition: p starts a Cunningham chain of the first kind of length at least 4.

tag_registry.label: Mersenne exponent
tag_registry.definition: 2^p - 1 is prime. Only 52 are known; this lists those below the horizon.

tag_registry.label: Fermat prime
tag_registry.definition: p = 2^(2^k) + 1. Only five are known.

tag_registry.label: Proth prime
tag_registry.definition: p = k*2^n + 1 with k odd and k < 2^n.

tag_registry.label: Cuban prime
tag_registry.definition: p = (x^3 - y^3)/(x - y) with y = x - 1 or y = x - 2.

tag_registry.label: Fibonacci prime
tag_registry.definition: p is a Fibonacci number.

tag_registry.label: Lucas prime
tag_registry.definition: p is a Lucas number.

tag_registry.label: Pell prime
tag_registry.definition: p is a Pell number.

tag_registry.label: Motzkin prime
tag_registry.definition: p is a Motzkin number.

tag_registry.label: Bell prime
tag_registry.definition: p is a Bell number.

tag_registry.label: Newman-Shanks-Williams prime
tag_registry.definition: p is an NSW number.

tag_registry.label: Repunit prime
tag_registry.definition: p is a base-10 repunit.

tag_registry.label: Pythagorean prime
tag_registry.definition: p = 4k + 1; equivalently p is a sum of two squares.

tag_registry.label: Gaussian prime
tag_registry.definition: p = 4k + 3; p stays prime in Z[i].

tag_registry.label: Eisenstein prime
tag_registry.definition: p = 3k + 2; p stays prime in the Eisenstein integers.

tag_registry.label: Palindromic prime
tag_registry.definition: p reads the same reversed.

tag_registry.label: Emirp
tag_registry.definition: p reversed is a different prime.

tag_registry.label: Circular prime
tag_registry.definition: every cyclic rotation of p's digits is prime.

tag_registry.label: Permutable prime
tag_registry.definition: every permutation of p's digits is prime.

tag_registry.label: Left-truncatable prime
tag_registry.definition: deleting leading digits one at a time leaves a prime every time.

tag_registry.label: Right-truncatable prime
tag_registry.definition: deleting trailing digits one at a time leaves a prime every time.

tag_registry.label: Two-sided prime
tag_registry.definition: left- and right-truncatable at once. Exactly 15 exist.

tag_registry.label: Strobogrammatic prime
tag_registry.definition: p reads the same rotated 180 degrees.

tag_registry.label: Repdigit prime
tag_registry.definition: all of p's digits are equal.

tag_registry.label: Prime-digit prime
tag_registry.definition: every digit of p is itself prime (2, 3, 5, 7).

tag_registry.label: Additive prime
tag_registry.definition: p's digit sum is prime.

tag_registry.label: Happy prime
tag_registry.definition: iterating sum-of-squared-digits from p reaches 1.

tag_registry.label: Delicate prime
tag_registry.definition: changing any single digit of p produces a composite.

tag_registry.label: Undulating prime
tag_registry.definition: p's digits alternate ababab... with a != b.

tag_registry.label: Plateau prime
tag_registry.definition: p's interior digits are equal and exceed its equal end digits.

tag_registry.label: Depression prime
tag_registry.definition: p's interior digits are equal and fall below its equal end digits.

tag_registry.label: Super-prime
tag_registry.definition: p is the n-th prime and n is itself prime.

tag_registry.label: Ramanujan prime
tag_registry.definition: the smallest R with pi(x) - pi(x/2) >= n for all x >= R.

tag_registry.label: Chen prime
tag_registry.definition: p + 2 is prime or a product of two primes.

tag_registry.label: Lucky prime
tag_registry.definition: p survives the lucky-number sieve as well as the prime sieve.

tag_registry.label: Decade prime
tag_registry.definition: p is the 10^k-th prime.

tag_registry.label: First prime of its digit width
tag_registry.definition: p is the smallest prime with its number of digits.

tag_registry.label: Last prime of its digit width
tag_registry.definition: p is the largest prime with its number of digits.

tag_registry.label: Wieferich prime
tag_registry.definition: 2^(p-1) = 1 mod p^2. Only two are known below 2^64.

tag_registry.label: Wilson prime
tag_registry.definition: (p-1)! = -1 mod p^2. Only three are known.

tag_registry.label: Wolstenholme prime
tag_registry.definition: binomial(2p-1, p-1) = 1 mod p^4. Only two are known.

tag_registry.label: Wall-Sun-Sun prime
tag_registry.definition: p^2 divides the Fibonacci number F(p - (5|p)). None is known to exist.

tag_registry.label: Stern prime
tag_registry.definition: p is not the sum of a smaller prime and twice a nonzero square.

tag_registry.label: Unique-period prime
tag_registry.definition: no other prime shares the period length of 1/p.

tag_registry.label: Fortunate prime
tag_registry.definition: p is the Fortunate number of some primorial.

tag_registry.label: Irregular prime
tag_registry.definition: p divides the numerator of some Bernoulli number B_2k, 2k < p - 1.

tag_registry.label: Full reptend prime
tag_registry.definition: 10 is a primitive root mod p; 1/p has maximal period p - 1.

tag_registry.label: Era generator
tag_registry.definition: p generates a primorial era boundary (CONCEPT.md SS7).

vanity_registry.label: Culturally loaded
vanity_registry.note: A small fixed set with demonstrable willingness-to-pay in every other digital-scarcity market: 42, 69, 420, 666, 777, 911, 1337, 8008, 80085, 90210, 1234, 12345.

vanity_registry.label: Repdigit
vanity_registry.note: All digits equal: 11, 777, 8888. The single most requested shape in every phone-number and licence-plate market there is.

vanity_registry.label: Round-number neighbour
vanity_registry.note: Within 3 of a power of ten. 1009 is the first prime past 1000 and that is why anyone wants it.

vanity_registry.label: Birth year
vanity_registry.note: 1930-2026. The largest identifiable cohort of vanity buyers, and the only one whose size can be estimated from demographics.

vanity_registry.label: Year
vanity_registry.note: 1000-2100 outside the birth-year band. Anniversaries, foundings, and the numbers people already put on things.

vanity_registry.label: Sequential digits
vanity_registry.note: Strictly ascending or descending by one: 4567, 98765.

vanity_registry.label: Date-shaped
vanity_registry.note: Six digits that parse as DDMMYY or MMDDYY. This is the single largest rule-expressible vanity cohort on the line -- roughly 22,000 numbers between 100,000 and 404,000 are somebody's birthday, anniversary, or the day they shipped something. It is also the cohort the flat 1 GRAM price gives away for free.

vanity_registry.label: Palindrome
vanity_registry.note: Priced again here, separately from its rarity, because palindromes sell on how they look and not on how rare they are.
